transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Morgan (Head of ML, Cobalt), Diego Ramirez (Infra Eng), Nina Park (Product Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, brief):
Cobalt Fintech is evaluating Redwood for latency-sensitive inference for several low-latency customer-facing features (fraud scoring, realtime assistant). Primary concerns: p95 latency SLAs, sustained concurrency (50-200 concurrent sessions), streaming support for partial output, cost tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Agreed to run benchmarks with sample prompts and provided telemetry. Next: pricing + benchmark plan + traces.

Topics: Latency targets (p95), concurrency, streaming token/sec benchmarks, model choices (LlamaX/Redwood-verified), Dedicated sizing, VPC/KMS/security.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Leah Morgan: Leah here. Head of ML at Cobalt.
[00:10] Diego Ramirez: Diego, infra.
[00:12] Nina Park: Nina, product.
[00:15] Ravi Patel: Ravi from Redwood, SE.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great. The goal today is quick discovery on latency and throughput requirements and discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private options. We'll ask about p95 targets, concurrency, streaming, and the workloads to size a benchmark.
[00:35] Leah Morgan: Cool. High level: we have two main use cases. One is a realtime assistant in our trader UI where we need very low latency completions for short prompts (~20-50 tokens output). The second is fraud scoring which runs many concurrent requests with ~100-300 tokens. Both need strong p95s and predictable tail behavior.
[00:54] Diego Ramirez: To add: infra constraint — we run in GCP us-west, prefer a VPC peering option or private deployment for regulated data. We're evaluating hosted first but Dedicated or Private if we need isolation. Also we operate at bursts: baseline ~200 req/s but can spike to 800 qps for short windows.
[01:15] Ravi Patel: Helpful. When you say p95 for the assistant, what numbers are you targeting?
[01:20] Leah Morgan: For the assistant, p95 under 250ms would be ideal. For fraud scoring, p95 under 700ms for typical 150-token runs, and we want token/sec throughput high enough to handle the spikes.
[01:34] Maya Chen: Got it. 250ms p95 for short completions is pretty strict but we've seen it with Dedicated infra and aggressive batching controls. For hosted we typically quote p95 in the 200-600ms range depending on model and request size; Dedicated gives tighter SLOs.
[01:52] Diego Ramirez: What hardware does Redwood Dedicated use? GPUs, memory? We're trying to map to our expected token/sec.
[01:59] Ravi Patel: Dedicated uses NVIDIA H100 and A100 pools depending on the model; we provide reserved GPU pools. We also support CPU-only smaller models but for your p95 goals H100 is the recommendation. For model variants we can run quantized weights to improve throughput.
[02:20] Nina Park: Ok. For streaming, we need partial tokens as they generate in the UI. Does Redwood support streaming and what's the cost/latency implication?
[02:27] Maya Chen: Yes streaming is supported across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Streaming can actually reduce perceived latency for the user since you can show partial tokens early; end-to-end p95 is still measured to completion unless you define custom SLOs on first-token. There is some overhead for many small streaming messages but it's usually negligible if batching is tuned.
[02:45] Leah Morgan: We're also sensitive to cost. If Dedicated with reserved capacity is way more expensive than hosted, we might accept slightly worse p95 during spikes. Can you give rough unit economics guidelines?
[02:55] Ravi Patel: Sure — rough rules: hosted is pay-as-you-go and often cheaper for bursty low baseline loads; Dedicated is better for predictable sustained throughput and gives lower p95 and cost per token. We'll include a cost comparison in the pricing doc.
[03:12] Diego Ramirez: On security we need SOC2, SSO, SAML, KMS integration. Also audit logs and ability to bring our own key material.
[03:20] Maya Chen: We have SOC2 Type II, SSO / SAML, RBAC and KMS/HSM options for Private deployments. Hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys via KMS integrations depending on the contract. We'll send the security pack.
[03:34] Ravi Patel: Back to latency — can you share current production numbers (p50/p95), avg tokens/request, and concurrency distribution?
[03:41] Diego Ramirez: We'll pull that. Current service mixes show avg tokens per request ~90, median latency ~120ms (but that's for our in-house microservice), p95 is spiking to 1.2s under load. Concurrency for the endpoint is generally 150-220, bursts to 700.
[03:59] Nina Park: Our UX team says anything beyond ~500ms is noticeable. So the trader assistant needs special handling.
[04:06] Leah Morgan: We also plan to experiment with streaming first-token SLOs (like 120ms first-byte). Can Redwood measure first-token latency separately?
[04:15] Ravi Patel: Yes, we can instrument first-token and end-to-end latencies in our Console. We also expose token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards for tracing regressions.
[04:30] Maya Chen: For the bench plan, Ravi, maybe outline what we need: sample prompt set, concurrency patterns, sequence lengths, desired SLO, and whether streaming is enabled. Then we can run hosted smoke tests and a Dedicated pilot.
[04:43] Ravi Patel: I'll draft that. For benchmarking, are you comfortable sharing a set of representative prompts? Mask PII if needed.
[04:50] Leah Morgan: Yes. We'll sanitize and share. We'll also share the workload distribution: 70% short assistant (<50 tokens), 30% scoring (100-300 tokens).
[05:02] Diego Ramirez: One technical Q: how does Redwood handle KV cache and prefix caching for similar repeated prompts — can that reduce token/sec cost and improve tail latency?
[05:10] Ravi Patel: We support KV cache and prefix caching. For high-repetition prompts we can cache keys to avoid recomputing the full context, which reduces p95 and cost. We'll capture typical cache hit rates during the benchmark.
[05:25] Nina Park: Any gotchas with streaming + batching? i.e. does batching delay first-token?
[05:30] Ravi Patel: There's a tradeoff: larger batches improve throughput but increase first-token latency. We have batching policies you can tune — max wait time and dynamic batching based on request size. For your assistant use-case we'd tune for low max-wait (like 5-10ms) and higher concurrency to keep throughput.
[05:48] Leah Morgan: For fraud scoring we want to prioritize throughput. Which model quantizations give best token/sec on H100?
[05:55] Ravi Patel: For H100, 3-bit/4-bit quantized LlamaX variants and optimized kernels give much better token/sec. We can provide recommended quantization profiles per model; Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization based on your evals.
[06:10] Diego Ramirez: How do you handle fallback when Dedicated capacity is saturated? We can't have failed scoring in production.
[06:16] Maya Chen: We support smart routing and automatic fallback — you can fallback to hosted pool or a lower-cost model variant. Also can do degraded mode with shorter max tokens or cached responses.
[06:28] Nina Park: For the pilot we're thinking 2-4 hours of sustained load tests, plus some spike tests. Is that sufficient?
[06:34] Ravi Patel: That will give us decent numbers. For p95 stability we prefer longer runs (30-60 minutes sustained) plus spike windows; but 2-4 hours total with repeated windows works too.
[06:47] Leah Morgan: Can you produce p95 breakdowns by endpoint and by token position (start vs tail)?
[06:54] Ravi Patel: Yes, our Console traces per-token latency and we can export p95 by route, model, and token index.
[07:02] Diego Ramirez: For Private deployments, what's the timeline for an on-prem install? We're subject to audits and might prefer Private for PII workloads.
[07:09] Maya Chen: Private tends to be 6-10 weeks depending on network and certs; Dedicated is faster since it's Redwood-hosted but in your VPC. We'll include timeline variations in the doc.
[07:22] Nina Park: Any limits on streaming concurrency? If 200 traders all streaming partial responses is that a problem?
[07:29] Ravi Patel: It's a load on the connection layer but the serving runtime handles it; we'd size the pool and set connection multiplexing accordingly. We typically recommend dedicated TLS termination and autoscaling rules.
[07:44] Maya Chen: Let's talk numbers — Diego you said current p95 spikes to 1.2s. If we take a target of p95 250ms for assistant and 700ms for scoring, Ravi can propose Dedicated pool size.
[07:55] Diego Ramirez: Happy to see what you propose. Also cost threshold: we want the Dedicated monthly cost not to exceed our current infra spend for this feature by more than 30%.
[08:04] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll include a cost model and options: Dedicated reserved, Dedicated with burst, or Hosted with burst-through Dedicated fallback.
[08:16] Ravi Patel: For the benchmark scripts we'll need: concurrency curve (baseline + spikes), distribution of tokens, whether to enable streaming, and the SLOs. We'll also instrument Prometheus/Jaeger endpoints if you want to compare.
[08:32] Leah Morgan: We'll provide that. One more question — how do you measure token/sec? Is it per-GPU or cluster-wide?
[08:40] Ravi Patel: Both. We measure token/sec per-GPU and aggregate cluster token/sec. We'll report tokens/sec at p50/p95 during the runs.
[08:51] Nina Park: Any experience with cold-starts/prefetch for KV cache? We sometimes see cold tail spikes after redeploys.
[08:58] Ravi Patel: Yes. We recommend warmup runs and persistent cache warming strategies. For Dedicated we can pin model instances to avoid cold-starts.
[09:10] Diego Ramirez: For the fraud scoring model, we currently use a quantized T5-like model served on Triton. Are there migration considerations?
[09:18] Ravi Patel: We can onboard Triton models; but migrating to Redwood runtime may give better batching and kernel selection across sequences. We'll do compatibility checks in the POC.
[09:30] Maya Chen: Quick recap: Redwood will send pricing + Dedicated sizing. We will run a benchmark plan after Cobalt shares prompts and traces. Action items...
[09:40] Leah Morgan: Sounds good.
[09:42] Diego Ramirez: Agreed.
[09:44] Nina Park: Thanks, we'll get the artifacts over.
[09:46] Ravi Patel: I'll follow up with the benchmark outline.
[09:48] Maya Chen: Great. We'll schedule the pilot for the week of 2026-03-30 pending your trace dump.
